title: 2000 AMC 8 Problem 16
statement: In order for Mateen to walk a kilometer (\(1000\) meters) in his rectangular backyard, he must walk the length \(25\) times or walk its perimeter \(10\) times. What is the area of Mateen’s backyard in square meters?

solutions.text:
We can see that the length is \(1000 \div 25 = 40\) meters, and the perimeter is \(1000 \div 10 = 100\) meters.

Note that the perimeter is \(2\) times the sum of the length and width.

This means that the width is \[100 \div 2 - 40 = 10\] meters, and the area is \[40 \cdot 10 = 400\] square meters.

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: The length comes from walking it \(25\) times
The perimeter comes from walking it \(10\) times
